html:
1What the exam is

The AI-901 exam is the current exam for the Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals certification. It is for people at the beginning of an AI solution development career. You need conceptual knowledge of AI solutions in Azure, foundational technical skills to work with them, Python syntax, and familiarity with Azure resources.

Important. The older exam AI-900 was retired on June 30, 2026. If a book, video or practice test says AI-900, its content is out of date: it did not cover building with Microsoft Foundry, which is more than half of AI-901.

Fact Value
Passing score 700 or more
Languages English first; other languages follow about eight weeks later
Retirement date none announced on the exam page
Duration, number of questions, price [Verify live] not on the pages this course was built from: confirm on the exam page. The price depends on the country or region.
Note

. Most questions cover generally available features. The exam may include Preview features if they are commonly used, so read the product names in this course as "current at the time of writing" and check Microsoft Learn before you book.

Exam tip

. If a study resource says AI-900, it is out of date: the current exam is AI-901, and more than half of it is about building with Microsoft Foundry.

2The two skill areas

Skill area Weight What it asks
Identify AI concepts and capabilities 40–45% Responsible AI, how generative models work, choosing models and settings, and recognizing AI workloads
Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry 55–60% Prompts, deploying and chatting with a model, the SDK, agents, text and speech, vision and image generation, information extraction

The second area is the bigger one, and it is hands-on in spirit: you must recognize what a small Python program does and which Foundry feature it uses. You do not need to memorize long code.

3Where each skill lives in this course

Modules Skill area Topics
1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Concepts and capabilities responsible AI; generative models; models and parameters; workloads; capabilities
6, 7, 8, 9 Foundry: generative AI and agents prompts; portal; SDK chat client; agents
10, 11, 12 Foundry: text, speech, vision, extraction text and speech apps; vision and image generation; Content Understanding
13 Both exam technique and final review

4How to read the exam wording

Word in the study guide What you must be able to do
Describe Explain what it is and what it is for
Identify Pick the right option for a described need
Create Know the steps or the settings that produce the result
Deploy, build Recognize the portal steps or the code that does it
Interpret Read what a request or output means

5A repeatable way to answer a question

  1. Read the last sentence first to see what is asked.
  2. Find the key need: text, speech, image, document, agent, safety, cost.
  3. Name the workload and drop options from other workloads.
  4. Pick the most specific service or feature for the need.
  5. Read code questions line by line: client creation, the call, the input, the output.
  6. Mark and move on if two options remain after a minute.

6A study plan

Step What to do Modules
1 Learn the ideas: responsible AI, how generative models work, models and parameters 1–3
2 Learn the workloads and what each AI capability does 4–5
3 Learn Foundry from prompts to agents 6–9
4 Learn the services behind text, speech, vision and extraction 10–12
5 Review with the cards and practice questions 13

Spaced review: answer each module's recall questions from memory, then check. Repeat each Quick Reference Card the next day and again after a week.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors finds a study book for "AI-900" in a shop. What should the team know before using it?

  • AAI-900 is the current exam, so the book is still fine to use
  • BAI-900 and AI-901 are the same exam, only the name was changed
  • CAI-900 now covers only Microsoft Foundry and nothing else
  • DAI-900 was retired on June 30, 2026, and AI-901 is the current exam
Show the answer

Answer: D. The study guide states that AI-900 was retired on June 30, 2026. AI-901 is the exam for the Azure AI Fundamentals certification.

S2Which skill area carries the larger weight in AI-901?

  • AImplement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry, at 55–60%
  • BIdentify AI concepts and capabilities, at 40–45%
  • CBoth skill areas carry exactly the same weight in the exam
  • DResponsible AI alone carries the largest weight of all topics
Show the answer

Answer: A. Implementing AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry is 55–60%, the larger area.

S3A candidate reads the skill "Create a lightweight chat client application by using the Foundry SDK". What is expected?

  • AMemorize every method of every SDK and recite it from memory
  • BBuild a physical datacenter for the AI solution
  • CRecognize what a short Python program does and which Foundry feature it calls
  • DOnly describe the history of AI and its famous researchers
Show the answer

Answer: C. The exam checks that you understand small applications and the Foundry features they use, not long memorized code.

S4What is the passing score of the AI-901 exam?

  • A500
  • B600
  • C800
  • D700
Show the answer

Answer: D. A score of 700 or greater is required to pass.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Which exam replaced AI-900?

Show the answer

AI-901.

R2Name the two skill areas and their weights.

Show the answer

Identify AI concepts and capabilities (40–45%) and Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%).

R3What score passes?

Show the answer

700 or more.

R4Which programming language does the exam expect you to read?

Show the answer

Python.

R5Which part of a question do you read first?

Show the answer

The last sentence.

R6Can the exam include Preview features?

Show the answer

Yes, if they are commonly used.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam AI-901 for Azure AI Fundamentals; AI-900 retired June 30, 2026; pass at 700
Skill areas concepts and capabilities 40–45%; implement with Microsoft Foundry 55–60%
Audience beginning of an AI solution development career; Python syntax and Azure resources
Method last sentence, key need, name the workload, most specific service, read code line by line, mark and move on
